answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A voyage delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A copper check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A kernel penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 4065 identities need 4065 bonds of 24 tokens, 8879 dollars of hardware and 33 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
